articles.title: Brazil’s new curtailment rules unlikely to revive utility-scale solar investment
articles.summary:
Large-scale solar developers in Brazil have received two updates on past and future generation curtailment. Curtailment rates of around 25%, combined with uncertainty over compensation, have frequently been cited as reasons for developers to surrender project authorizations. While the new curtailment rules offer greater certainty and predictability, a recovery in investment will depend on other factors.

In 2026 alone, developers surrendered authorizations for 923 solar projects in Brazil, representing more than 40.6 GW of capacity and BRL 134 billion ($26.3 billion) in lost investment, according to a study by the Brazilian Solar Photovoltaic Energy Association (ABsolar). articles.summary:
Sineng Electric is supporting Zambia’s renewable energy development with its high-efficiency central inverters deployed at the 100 MW Maamba PV Power Station in Southern Province, which was commissioned on September 24, 2026. The project will add utility-scale solar generation capacity to the national grid, supporting the diversification of Zambia’s energy mix and enhancing its long-term energy security.

Located in Maamba, Sinazongwe District, the project is being constructed by Sinoma Energy Conservation Ltd., which serves as the engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contractor. articles.title: Solar power provides new business opportunities in the south‑western part of Burkina Faso
articles.summary:
A female small business owner and customer of one of our financed portfolio companies in Burkina Faso, Oolu by Ignite, can now contribute to the household economy thanks to an installed off-grid solar kit that provides electricity for running a refrigerator.

In a neighbourhood of Bobo-Dioulasso, where grid infrastructure exists but electricity has yet to arrive, Tinta Setou and her family used to rely on charcoal, gas and small solar lamps for their daily energy needs. The lamps provided only a few hours of light each night, limiting household activities and business opportunities.

articles.title: Africa has seen oil shocks before. Why 2026 could be the turning point for clean energy
articles.summary:
Africa has been here before. Oil climbs above $100, import bills balloon, Finance ministers across the continent convene emergency sessions, and somewhere in a development bank boardroom, a clean energy investment pipeline gets quietly deprioritised while everyone waits for the price to come back down.

In 2008, the global financial crisis interrupted a Brent spike that had touched $147. articles.title: Selous solar project for Afrochine’s smelter gets a parent-company payment guarantee
articles.summary:
A direct agreement signed in Harare puts Zhejiang Dinson Holding Group behind the electricity payments its subsidiary Afrochine Smelting owes the 115MW Selous Solar PV Project in Zimbabwe, adding security for lenders led by the Trade and Development Bank as the plant heads for commissioning in 2027.

A US$87.5m long-term facility led by the Trade and Development Bank and a US$65m bridge from Sinohydro Leasing International, a PowerChina subsidiary, are financing the 115MW Selous Solar PV Project in Zimbabwe, where a direct agreement signed in Harare last week puts Zhejiang Dinson Holding Group behind the electricity payments its local subsidiary, Afrochine Smelting, owes the developer and its lenders.
